spam.title: Chat protection

spam.scoresHint: These are independent behavior probabilities; they do not add up to 100%. Safe means none of your selected behaviors.
spam.modelHint: Free uses Span-1 with no AI credits. Premium and Pro use the more accurate Jev, which uses AI credits for each review; if credits run out, it falls back to Span-1 Lite, which can be less accurate on complex or ambiguous text.

Adjust a few percentage points at a time and check several examples, including the languages used in your chat. You can choose any value from 0–100%, including decimals.

duelWidget.stepWinner: Fighters take turns: usually a normal attack, sometimes a heavy one, rarely a special, and any hit can crit for double damage. Sometimes the defender's skill (Shield Wall, Ghost Step or Arcane Ward) stops a normal attack or cuts a heavy one by 80%; specials shatter it at full damage. Fighters may heal up to 5 times, and blocking can chain into a combo heal, and anyone can strike twice in a row. Very rarely a fighter unleashes an unblockable one-shot ultimate (much more often when the enraged streamer fights). The first to 0 HP loses, and chat gets the winner.

observability.title: Observability
observability.intro: See where time goes, what is waiting, and which services need attention.
observability.private: Access is granted separately from employee or channel permissions.
observability.truncated: This view reached its row limit. Narrow the time range or filters before comparing totals.
observability.chartLabel: HTTP and chat processing rate over time. Exact values are available below.
observability.chartNote: Rates average completed operations over each bucket. Gaps mean no observations; the newest bucket may be incomplete.
observability.noData: No observations in this range yet. Data appears as the services handle traffic.
observability.contributionNote: Observed workload, not an allocation of shared CPU or RAM. Select a channel to filter the view.
observability.noTransitions: No stream transitions observed in this range.
observability.lifecycleNote: Latest observed transition per channel and type. Compare traffic before and after; timing alone does not prove the cause.
observability.queueNote: Waiting depth and age are sampled. Queue wait, handler execution, and time until ready are separate timings. Check the observation time before treating a value as current.
observability.timingNote: Durations are elapsed time, including waits. HTTP client timings end at response headers. Database and cache operations are counted separately.
observability.resourceNote: Database RAM, internal cache occupancy, and disk storage are distinct. Values show their last observation time. Shared resources are visible only with system-wide access.
observability.unavailable: Analytics is temporarily unavailable. Existing data may be stale.
observability.partialTrace: Partial trace: only retained operations within your access scope are shown.
observability.sampledTrace: Sampled trace. Overlapping bars run concurrently; their durations should not be added.
observability.traceNote: Normal traces are sampled at 1%. Slow operations and errors are retained within bounded limits. This list is not the source of request totals.
observability.noTraces: No retained traces in this range. Metrics still count all observed operations.
observability.logsNote: Structured warnings and errors from the application logger. Messages, request bodies, tokens, and chat text are excluded.
observability.noLogs: No retained warnings or errors in this range.
observability.accessNote: Invite a Twitch account to analytics without granting employee access. Only the owner can manage these grants.
observability.scopeNote: Empty scope fields grant access to all channels or services. Viewers see metrics; investigators can also read sanitized logs and traces.
observability.confirmGrant: Grant analytics access to Twitch user
observability.confirmRevoke: Revoke analytics access for Twitch user
observability.invalidGrant: Check the user ID, scope, and expiration date.
